checkpoints.notes: 5 new concepts brainstormed and scored (Ink Territory, Echo Maze, Tether Duel, Pulse Runner, plus an Orbit Duel refinement option carried from Cycle 1 follow-ups). Ink Territory selected; Echo Maze as fallback.

Single-file HTML5 canvas + grid architecture defined: fixed-timestep tick loop, wet-trail/territory-seal rules, death/respawn rules, debug hooks (setTimeRemaining, tick()) planned up front to close Cycle 1's win-condition testing gap.

Self-contained playable prototype implemented per design.md: grid movement, wet-trail/territory-seal, death/respawn, HUD, restart, and window.__inkTerritory debug hooks (tick(), setTimeRemaining, reset()).

Automated Playwright/headless-Chromium test suite: 8/8 PASS, including a full win-condition + restart end-to-end test (closing the exact gap Cycle 1 flagged as a follow-up). Found and fixed one testability gap during testing: added a setPaused() debug hook so scripted tick() sequences aren't perturbed by the game's real-time auto-forward movement between Playwright round-trips.

followUps: Human/manual playtest of Ink Territory for feel/balance tuning (TICK_MS move speed, RESPAWN_MS).
Automated test for the head-on-collision rule (both players landing on the same cell in one tick) -- verified by code review only so far.

Orbit Duel's Cycle 1 follow-ups remain open and undeferred further: manual playtest, automated win-condition test (now demonstrated achievable -- see Ink Territory's setTimeRemaining/tick hooks as a reusable pattern), and a possible simple AI opponent.
Consider the design doc's documented scope cut (Qix-style enclosed-area flood fill, vs. path-only sealing) as a candidate enhancement if Ink Territory is revisited in a future cycle.
budgetNotes: Cycle 2 completed in the same single-session, no-subagent-fan-out style as Cycle 1 to conserve budget. Cycle 1's full history preserved below under history[0] for audit. Cycle 2 completed fully within budget with no usage-limit warning encountered.
